comparator.name: Human Geography and Planning
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026-2027 Faculty of Spatial Sciences TER defines one 180-EC programme with a fixed 60-EC first year, a 60-EC second year containing one 5-EC restricted elective, and a 60-EC third year containing 30 EC of genuine elective, minor, exchange or internship space. Healthy Ageing is instantiated by the neutral official-order tie-break because it appears first in the TER list of four equally weighted restricted electives; no UCR-fit consideration enters that choice. The two-part Bachelor's Project is represented once at its combined 15 EC. The 30-EC third-year choice space remains open rather than being filled with invented subjects.
components: Reflecting on Human Geography and Planning
First-listed option selected by neutral official-order tie-break from Healthy Ageing, Population and Development, Real Estate Principles, and North America: A Regional Perspective.
Genuine approved choice space preserved without inventing a student selection.
The TER schedules 5 EC in semester 2a and 10 EC in semester 2b; represented once at the combined credit load.
Geography, Planning and the European Union

alternatives.label: Human geography, planning & spatial sustainability
alternatives.concept: Combines social-spatial analysis of people, places, inequality and regional change with planning governance, environmental systems, spatial data, economics and applied sustainability research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates human geography and planning questions with spatial-environmental methods and sustainability, without claiming a dedicated professional planning degree.
progression: Social-science, sustainability, data and research foundations precede advanced urban inequality, environmental governance, earth observation, econometrics and applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Urban governance, housing & inclusive development
alternatives.concept: Organises sociology, politics, law, economics, psychology and communication around urban development, housing and land use, inequality, collaborative planning and the governance of sustainable and inclusive cities.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme centres institutional, distributive and political choices in urban development and housing while retaining social research and environmental policy.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces much of the earth-system, spatial-data and environmental-technology sequence with law, political institutions, diversity, communication, design and public decision-making. Ten courses differ, exceeding the 30-EC floor.
progression: Sociology, politics, law and research-method foundations precede comparative institutions, urban inequality, rights, governance, communication and advanced policy-facing study. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Globalisation, migration & regional inequality
alternatives.concept: Studies how globalisation, migration, political institutions, economic change, inequality, race, heritage and social movements shape regions and places across borders, supported by qualitative, quantitative and historical research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum shifts the spatial question to global connections, migration and uneven regional development without claiming a dedicated geography sequence.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most planning, design and environmental-technology content with empire, international relations, global political economy, migration-related inequality, race, heritage and transnational histories. It differs by at least nine courses from each earlier alternative.
progression: Sociology, politics, history and research foundations precede global political economy, international law, race, heritage, social movements and advanced transnational analysis. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates the target's social-spatial, planning, environmental and mixed-method core. Urban governance and globalisation/migration are separately evidenced by direct target interests and produce materially different curricula. All three are mechanically feasible and pairwise differ by at least nine courses, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: Groningen provides a continuous disciplinary sequence in human geography and planning, including dedicated GIS, population and rural geography, fieldwork, planning theory and dynamics, and a bachelor thesis. UCR can combine strong sociology, politics, economics, sustainability, environmental science, data and research courses, but the fixed Fall 2026 catalogue does not offer the same full geography-and-planning sequence. The UCR alternatives therefore cover related subjects and methods without claiming professional planning equivalence.
